To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the levels of calcium, sodium and magnesium are higher in the serum than in the plasma, and potassium level is lower in the serum than plasma.
the levels of major minerals like calcium, sodium, and potassium in plasma got altered significantly in the presence of heparin as well as EDTA, as anticoagulant, when compared with the serum levels.
heparin and Potassium EDTA (KEDTA) significantly influence the levels of calcium, sodium and potasium in plasma of different species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comparative analysis of the levels of calcium, sodium and Potassium in plasma and serum of human, elephant, dog, cattle, sheep and goat.
a comparative study of the effects of heparin, EDTA and serum on levels of major electrolyte minerals in plasma.
the influence of anticoagulant on the level of electrolytes in the plasma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
heparin is the best anticoagulant for the determination of the levels of major minerals in plasma.
the levels of calcium, sodium and potassiun in plasma were significantly influenced by the addition of anticoagulant.
heparin can be used as antico-agulant for the estimation of these electrolytes in the plasma of all the species studied, except human, whereas EDTA can be used for human blood plasma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

heparin is a better anticoagulant than EDTA, as far as the levels of calcium, sodium and potasium in the plasma are concerned, and hence it is preferable to EDTA for blood sampling for clinical purposes.
heparin can be safely used as an anticoagulant to study the electrolyte status of blood plasma.
heparin is a better anticoagulant for blood samples for the estimation of electrolyte levels in plasma, than EDTA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
heparin is the better anticoagulant than EDTA, when it comes to measuring the levels of these major electrolytes in blood.
heparin is a better anticoagulant than EDTA in preserving the levels of calcium, sodium and potasium in blood plasma.

the use of anticoagulant is inevitable in blood collection and the choice of anticoagulation is a very important factor that should be taken into account while analyzing the blood samples for the levels of minerals.
